title: Formalisation of the theory of real closed fields in Lean 4.

source.citation: Bochnak-Coste-Roy, Real Algebraic Geometry (Springer 1998); Knebusch-Scheiderer, Real Algebra (Springer 2022); Jacobson, Basic Algebra I and II (Dover 2012 reprint); Lam, Orderings, valuations and quadratic forms (AMS CBMS 1984)
source.scope: textbook theory of ordered/real closed fields, real closures, Artin-Schreier
source.evidence: Blueprint intro: "We synthesise material from \cite{Bochnak1998}, \cite{Knebusch2022}, \cite{Jacobson2012I} and \cite{Jacobson2012II} as convenient."

edge_sample.source_text: definition : A real closed field $F$ is a real field such that \begin{enumerate} \item for all $x$ in $F$, either $x$ or $-x$ is a square in $F$, and \item every odd-degree polynomial over $F$ has a root in $F$. \end{enumerate}
edge_sample.target_text: theorem : The only finite extensions of $R$ are $R$ itself and $R(i)$.

edge_sample.source_text: lemma : Let $F$ be an ordered field, and let $K/F$ be a field extension. Suppose that there is an $F$-linear functional $\pi:K\to F$ such that, for all $x\in K$, $\pi(x^2)\geq0$. Then there is a field ordering on $K$ making $K/F$ ordered.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : Let $\pi:F(\sqrt{a})\to F$ be the projection induced by the $F$-basis $\{1,\sqrt{a}\}$. For $x,y\in F$, we have $\pi((x+y\sqrt{a})^2)=x^2+ay^2\geq0$. We are done by Lemma \ref{lem:ext_ord_functional_suff}.

edge_sample.source_text: corollary : Suppose $R$ is a field with nontrivial algebraic closure $R(i)$. Then $R$ is real closed.
